title: Change Your Questions, Change Your Life

questions.q: What separates learner questions from judger questions?
a: Learner questions open possibility; judger questions assign blame
Learner questions are longer; judger questions are brief
Learner questions seek facts; judger questions seek feelings
Learner questions suit others; judger questions suit yourself
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts questions that create solutions and win-win relations with ones that leave you stuck in judgment.

questions.q: What is a switching question meant to do?
a: Move you from judgment into a learning mindset
Prove that the other person is wrong
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes switching questions as a life preserver that flips you out of the judger pit.

questions.q: What does the ABCC Choice Process ask you to do first?
a: Ask yourself whether you are judging
questions.why: The overview outlines the process: notice judgment, pause and get curious, then pick a learner question.

questions.q: What signals that you have slipped into judger mode?
a: An urge to ask more questions
questions.why: Lesson 2 says anger and frustration alert your inner observer that it is time to switch questions.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the twelve learner questions?
a: Why am I such a failure?
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists that question among twelve prompts meant to open up possibility and creative thinking.
